scenarios.name: Ignis Sentinel: Global Wildfire & Biosphere Early Warning
scenarios.mission_objective: Monitor global terrestrial wildfire hotspots and deforestation fronts at high spatial and temporal resolution.

orbit_trajectory_options.name: Sun-Synchronous Noon/Midnight (SSO-550)
orbit_trajectory_options.pros: Consistent sunlit illumination for optical imagery, predictable ground pass scheduling over high-latitude stations (Svalbard/Troll).
orbit_trajectory_options.cons: Requires 35-minute eclipse battery survival every 95-minute orbit; moderate atmospheric drag.

orbit_trajectory_options.name: Dawn-Dusk Sun-Synchronous (SSO-650-DD)
orbit_trajectory_options.pros: Continuous solar panel illumination (near 0% eclipse), drastically reducing battery mass and thermal cycling.
orbit_trajectory_options.cons: Low sun-elevation angles produce heavy shadows on surface terrain; slightly degraded optical contrast.

orbit_trajectory_options.name: Mid-Inclination Low Earth Orbit (LEO-400-51deg)
orbit_trajectory_options.pros: High ground resolution (closer to surface), low launch insertion delta-V.
orbit_trajectory_options.cons: Zero coverage of polar/boreal forests; severe atmospheric drag requiring frequent propulsion stationkeeping burns.

environmental_challenges: Frequent Day-to-Night thermal cycling (15 to 16 eclipses per 24 hours)
Residual upper-atmospheric atomic oxygen erosion in LEO
South Atlantic Anomaly (SAA) radiation single-event upsets
failure_conditions: Battery State of Charge drops to 0% during an eclipse transit
Onboard solid-state memory buffer overflows (>100% capacity) dropping more than 50 GB of data
Orbital altitude decays below 220 km due to drag without propulsion recovery
optional_objectives: Zero-Propellant Survival: Complete the 180-day mission using only aerodynamic trim and magnetic torquers
High-Throughput Downlink: Transmit >1,000 GB of telemetry using Ka-band high-gain comms
Under-Budget Award: Complete mission under $12M total CapEx

viable_architectures.name: Agile 12U CubeSat Rideshare
viable_architectures.description: Utilizes standard 12U chassis, basic imager (INST-OPT-01), body panels, and S-band comms launched via low-cost ESPA rideshare slot. Low budget ($3.5M), high margin efficiency.
viable_architectures.subsystem_profile: STR-ALU-01 + INST-OPT-01 + EPS-SOL-01 + EPS-BAT-01 + ANT-S-01 + ADCS-RW-02

viable_architectures.name: Dedicated Sub-Meter Commercial SmallSat
viable_architectures.description: Uses Hexagonal CFRP bus, intermediate telescope (INST-OPT-02), deployable GaAs wings, and X-band horn launched on a dedicated micro-launcher. Delivers 5x higher science return at $24M cost.
viable_architectures.subsystem_profile: STR-CFRP-02 + INST-OPT-02 + EPS-SOL-02 + EPS-BAT-02 + ANT-X-02 + ADCS-RW-02 + PROP-HYD-02

scenarios.name: Selene Core: Lunar South Pole Volatile & Ice Prospector
scenarios.mission_objective: Map permanently shadowed craters (PSRs) at the lunar South Pole to quantify water-ice deposits and evaluate landing sites for human exploration.

orbit_trajectory_options.name: Low Lunar Polar Orbit (LLPO-100)
orbit_trajectory_options.pros: Uniform coverage of both lunar poles; maximum spatial resolution for radar altimeter.
orbit_trajectory_options.cons: Unstable over long durations due to lunar mascons (gravitational anomalies); requires active periodic stationkeeping.

orbit_trajectory_options.name: Frozen Elliptical Polar Orbit (FEPO 30x200)
orbit_trajectory_options.pros: Long-term orbital stability with minimal stationkeeping propellant; close periapsis passes over south pole.
orbit_trajectory_options.cons: Asymmetric resolution between northern and southern hemispheres.

environmental_challenges: Severe lunar thermal extremes: 390 K in full sun down to 40 K in permanently shadowed regions
Lunar mascon gravitational perturbations causing rapid orbital eccentricity growth
Occultations by the Moon causing 45-minute continuous communication blackouts with Earth on every orbit
failure_conditions: Propellant exhaustion prior to lunar orbit insertion (spacecraft flys by into heliocentric graveyard)
Lunar surface impact caused by uncorrected mascon orbit decay
Thermal freezing of propulsion fuel lines during long lunar night passes
optional_objectives: Gravitational Field Mapping: Detect 3 major subsurface mascons via Doppler tracking
Permanent Shadow Penetration: Complete 500 radar passes over Shackleton crater
Extended Operations: Maintain orbit for >365 days using electric propulsion

viable_architectures.name: High-Thrust Chemical Insertion Bus
viable_architectures.description: Utilizes hydrazine bipropellant for rapid Lunar Orbit Insertion (LOI) burn in 15 minutes, with heavy structural bus and X-band communication.
viable_architectures.subsystem_profile: STR-CFRP-02 + INST-OPT-02 + PROP-HYD-02 + EPS-SOL-02 + EPS-BAT-02 + ANT-X-02 + TCS-PIPE-02

viable_architectures.name: Solar Electric Spiral-In Explorer
viable_architectures.description: Uses Hall-effect electric propulsion with high Isp (1,850 s). Spirals slowly from high lunar orbit to 100 km over 45 days, saving massive propellant mass.
viable_architectures.subsystem_profile: STR-CFRP-02 + INST-OPT-02 + PROP-ION-03 + EPS-SOL-03 + EPS-BAT-03 + ANT-X-02 + TCS-PIPE-02

scenarios.name: Ares Echo: Mars Atmosphere & Subsurface Ice Mapper
scenarios.mission_objective: Conduct high-resolution atmospheric soundings and radar scans of Martian glacial sheets while acting as a telecom relay for future surface landers.

orbit_trajectory_options.name: Low-Mars Circular Sun-Synchronous (MO-300-SSO)
orbit_trajectory_options.pros: Optimal for continuous surface imaging and maximum lander relay contact passes; constant solar illumination time.
orbit_trajectory_options.cons: Demands massive delta-V insertion (or aerobraking over 4 months); atmospheric dust drag during global dust storms.

orbit_trajectory_options.name: Highly Elliptical Mars Insertion Orbit (HEMO 400x12000)
orbit_trajectory_options.pros: Saves >1,100 m/s in insertion propellant; broad hemispheric synoptic imaging at apoapsis.
orbit_trajectory_options.cons: Short nadir high-res observation windows at periapsis; highly variable communication link distances with surface assets.

environmental_challenges: Solar irradiance drops to 43% of Earth levels (~589 W/m²), requiring oversized solar panels
One-way communication light-time latency of 4 to 22 minutes (demands complete autonomous onboard fault recovery)
Global Martian dust storms coating solar arrays and heating the upper atmosphere
Interplanetary transit cruise phase lasting 7 to 9 months with deep-space cosmic radiation
failure_conditions: Critical onboard fault during Mars Orbit Insertion (MOI) burn causing mission loss
Failure to deploy solar arrays after cruise phase
Loss of autonomous lock due to ADCS star-tracker blinding during a solar particle event
Missed Earth launch window (incurs 26-month mission cancellation penalty)
optional_objectives: Lander Relay Pioneer: Transmit >500 GB of synthetic lander relay data back to Earth's Deep Space Network
Global Dust Storm Observer: Maintain full atmospheric monitoring through a category-5 planetary dust storm
Phobos Gravity Assist: Plan trajectory to perform a 50 km flyby of Phobos during insertion

viable_architectures.name: Deep-Space Chemical Flagship
viable_architectures.description: Heavy-lift launch directly to high C3, heavy isogrid bus (STR-ISO-03), massive bipropellant tank, Ka-band parabolic dish, and high-efficiency triple-junction tracking wings.
viable_architectures.subsystem_profile: STR-ISO-03 + INST-OPT-02 + PROP-HYD-02 + EPS-SOL-03 + EPS-BAT-03 + ANT-KA-03 + OBC-RAD-02 + ADCS-ST-03

viable_architectures.name: High-Efficiency Dual-Engine Hybrid
viable_architectures.description: Utilizes chemical propulsion for trans-Mars injection and initial capture, followed by low-thrust Xenon Hall electric propulsion to circularize orbit over 90 days, cutting wet mass by 40%.
viable_architectures.subsystem_profile: STR-CFRP-02 + INST-OPT-02 + PROP-ION-03 + EPS-SOL-03 + EPS-BAT-03 + ANT-X-02 + OBC-AI-03 + ADCS-RW-02

scenarios.name: Didymos Recon: Near-Earth Asteroid Kinetic Deflection Scout
scenarios.mission_objective: Rendezvous with a binary near-Earth asteroid system, measure orbital deflection properties, and conduct multispectral compositional surface analysis.

orbit_trajectory_options.name: Direct Heliocentric Hohmann Intercept
orbit_trajectory_options.pros: Short transit time (11 months); continuous direct communication visibility with Earth.
orbit_trajectory_options.cons: High hyperbolic excess velocity ($v_\infty$) requiring large terminal rendezvous braking burn.

orbit_trajectory_options.name: Earth Gravity Assist Resonant Trajectory (E-GART)
orbit_trajectory_options.pros: Saves >700 m/s delta-V by utilizing Earth swing-by 1 year after launch.
orbit_trajectory_options.cons: Extends flight time to 2.4 years; requires high navigation accuracy during Earth flyby.

environmental_challenges: Micro-gravity environment around asteroid (< 0.0001 m/s²), where solar radiation pressure dominates trajectory
Severe rotational tumbling of asteroid targets creating rapid shadow-crossing thermal shocks
Autonomous optical navigation required for close proximity proximity operations (< 1 km)
failure_conditions: Hyperbolic flyby without braking: relative velocity never drops below asteroid escape velocity
Spacecraft collision with asteroid during proximity mapping
Loss of attitude control due to reaction wheel momentum saturation in microgravity without thruster desaturation
optional_objectives: Sub-Kilometer Close Hover: Maintain autonomous stationkeeping at < 500 meters from asteroid surface for 30 days
Binary Mass Determination: Calculate secondary moonlet mass to within 3% accuracy
Sample Tag-and-Touch Simulation: Perform simulated surface touch maneuver without landing gear damage

viable_architectures.name: Solar Electric Ion Cruiser
viable_architectures.description: Equipped with Xenon Hall propulsion (`PROP-ION-03`) and articulated solar panels (`EPS-SOL-03`). Low wet mass, continuous low-thrust shaping for precise rendezvous.
viable_architectures.subsystem_profile: STR-CFRP-02 + INST-OPT-02 + INST-MAG-01 + PROP-ION-03 + EPS-SOL-03 + EPS-BAT-02 + ANT-X-02 + ADCS-ST-03

viable_architectures.name: Bipropellant Fast-Transit Interceptor
viable_architectures.description: Standard chemical spacecraft launched on dedicated Falcon 9. Higher propellant mass, but completes rendezvous in under 12 months.
viable_architectures.subsystem_profile: STR-ISO-03 + INST-OPT-02 + PROP-HYD-02 + EPS-SOL-02 + EPS-BAT-02 + ANT-X-02 + ADCS-ST-03

scenarios.name: Helios Voyager: Interstellar Boundary & Solar Storm Probe
scenarios.target_destination: Sun-Earth Lagrange L1 & Outer Heliopause Vector
scenarios.mission_objective: Measure solar wind dynamics, coronal mass ejections, and cosmic rays from an uninterrupted vantage point at Sun-Earth L1 before accelerating outward.

orbit_trajectory_options.name: Sun-Earth Lagrange L1 Halo Orbit
orbit_trajectory_options.pros: Zero eclipses ever (100% continuous solar power); uninterrupted line-of-sight to the Sun; constant Earth geometry.
orbit_trajectory_options.cons: Inherently unstable orbit (saddle point) requiring stationkeeping delta-V every 20 days; 1.5 million km comms distance.

orbit_trajectory_options.name: Earth-Trailing Heliocentric Drift (Spitzer-style)
orbit_trajectory_options.pros: Completely passive orbit; zero stationkeeping propulsion needed; zero thermal interference from Earth.
orbit_trajectory_options.cons: Distance to Earth increases by ~15 million km every year, causing severe RF link margin degradation over time.

environmental_challenges: Unmitigated deep-space radiation environment (cosmic rays, solar proton events)
Zero planetary magnetic field to aid in attitude desaturation (magnetorquers completely ineffective)
Extremely faint radio signal levels across 1.5 to 50 million kilometers
failure_conditions: Stationkeeping fuel exhaustion in L1 halo orbit, causing spacecraft to drift away uncontrollably
Single-Event Burnout of flight computer during a major Coronal Mass Ejection
Loss of high-gain antenna Earth-pointing lock with no omnidirectional link recovery
optional_objectives: Space Weather Real-Time Alert: Successfully downlink CME detection alert within 15 minutes of occurrence
Three-Year Uninterrupted Telemetry: Maintain 99.5% link uptime across 3 calendar years
Zero-Battery Operations: Operate the probe with minimal battery reserve utilizing continuous L1 solar flux

viable_architectures.name: High-Reliability Rad-Hard Monitor
viable_architectures.description: Utilizes BAE RAD750 processor (`OBC-RAD-02`), fluxgate magnetometer on deployable boom (`INST-MAG-01`), steerable Ka-band dish, and cold gas desaturation.
viable_architectures.subsystem_profile: STR-CFRP-02 + INST-MAG-01 + EPS-SOL-02 + EPS-BAT-02 + ANT-KA-03 + OBC-RAD-02 + PROP-CG-01 + ADCS-RW-02

viable_architectures.name: Micro-Probe Long-Baseline Fleet
viable_architectures.description: Compact bus with body-mounted arrays, low-power transmitters, and multi-year drift trajectory, minimizing overall mission lifecycle cost.
viable_architectures.subsystem_profile: STR-ALU-01 + INST-MAG-01 + EPS-SOL-01 + EPS-BAT-01 + ANT-X-02 + OBC-LEON-01 + ADCS-RW-02

scenarios.name: TerraLink Gateway: High-Throughput Geostationary Telecom Hub
scenarios.mission_objective: Provide continuous, high-availability multi-gigabit broadband and sovereign emergency communication relay over a designated continental landmass.

orbit_trajectory_options.name: Standard Geostationary Orbit (GEO-35786)
orbit_trajectory_options.pros: Satellite appears permanently stationary from the ground; zero ground antenna tracking required; 24/7 continuous coverage of 1/3 of Earth.
orbit_trajectory_options.cons: High launch energy / insertion delta-V required from GTO to GEO; high latency (~250 ms round trip); severe radiation environment (Van Allen outer belt).

orbit_trajectory_options.name: Inclined Geosynchronous Orbit (IGSO-35786-28deg)
orbit_trajectory_options.pros: Zero plane-change delta-V needed from Cape Canaveral GTO; higher daily elevation coverage over mid-to-high latitudes.
orbit_trajectory_options.cons: Ground ground-tracks trace a figure-8 figure; ground stations require active mechanical tracking antennas.

environmental_challenges: Intense outer Van Allen radiation belt electrons causing electrostatic surface charging
Bi-annual equinoctial eclipse seasons (up to 72 minutes of darkness per day for 45 consecutive days)
Lunar and solar gravitational perturbations demanding constant North-South inclination stationkeeping burns (~50 m/s per year)
failure_conditions: Exceeding allocated orbital slot box (±0.05°) violating ITU radio regulations and risking collision
Complete battery depletion during the critical 72-minute equinox midnight eclipse
Thermal runaway of high-power RF transponder amplifiers
optional_objectives: 15-Year Life Guarantee: Retain sufficient propellant reserve for 15 full years of operational stationkeeping
All-Electric Orbit Raising: Perform GTO-to-GEO transfer exclusively using Xenon Hall thrusters, saving >1,000 kg launch mass
Graveyard Disposal: Successfully boost spacecraft 300 km above GEO at end-of-life per IADC space debris guidelines

viable_architectures.name: Classic High-Thrust Bipropellant GEO Bus
viable_architectures.description: Uses heavy-lift launcher into GTO, onboard liquid apogee engine (hydrazine/NTO) for 3-day circularization, massive deployable solar arrays, and Ka-band reflector dishes.
viable_architectures.subsystem_profile: STR-ISO-03 + PROP-HYD-02 + EPS-SOL-03 + EPS-BAT-03 + ANT-KA-03 + TCS-PIPE-02 + ADCS-ST-03

viable_architectures.name: Modern All-Electric High-Throughput Satellite (HTS)
viable_architectures.description: Utilizes dual Xenon Hall electric thrusters (`PROP-ION-03`) for both GTO-to-GEO orbit raising and 15-year North-South stationkeeping, reducing launch mass by over 50%.
viable_architectures.subsystem_profile: STR-CFRP-02 + PROP-ION-03 + EPS-SOL-03 + EPS-BAT-03 + ANT-KA-03 + TCS-CRYO-03 + ADCS-ST-03
